verdictStatement: The repair Codex asked for is done exactly as specified. The governingSources note no longer routes a v4 reader to the obsolete v2 block; it now says d210f103… was the live digest at v2 authoring and that the current live digest is only at reMeasurementAtV3, the path is named on the closed roster, and it is recorded in the repair log — all three elements of Codex's minimumRepair. I tracked the offending sentence through the whole artifact: it survives at exactly three sites, and every one is benign — the attack instruction that hunts it, the historical v1 repair record where it was true when written, and the v3 repair entry that quotes it to say it no longer applies. The live pointer itself is clean, both reMeasurementAtV3 digests reproduce against live bytes, and every other dispatched attack fails: the DR-118 row is byte-exact at live file 08 line 300, no numeral is a threshold, DR-125 remains an OPEN activation gate, and fifteen substantive blocks are byte-identical to v3. What withholds acceptance is on the ledger side. This generation deletes two digest-pinned predecessor-verdict entries without disclosing the removal, and in the same breath books a carried finding that names one of the entries it just deleted.

A successor asked to fold the advisory cannot restore blockers [] to an entry that is not there; it would have to reconstruct the entry first, which the carry does not say.

coordinatorNote: The repair itself is clean and complete — Codex asked for three things and got all three, and I tracked the offending sentence through the entire artifact rather than checking only the field that was supposed to change. I also record that I passed this defect at v3 by treating an unchanged path as safe when a sibling path had moved around it; Codex was right and the miss is mine. What stops acceptance is a new problem on the ledger side rather than the contract side: v4 deletes the codexv1 and claude2v2 verdict pins without mentioning either removal in a repair log that has exactly one entry, and then books a carried finding that names codexv1 as its subject — so the artifact's own forward obligation points at something it just removed. Separately, the frozen Codex v3 verdict carries two findings and the ledger records one; in fairness the dispatch said the same, so that part looks inherited rather than concealed, and the missing advisory's substance does travel under my v3 id. Nothing here touches the contract: fifteen substantive blocks are byte-identical, the register row and remeasurement digests all reproduce, and provenance is recoverable one hop through basedOn. DR-118 stays DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, no threshold is minted, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
